# Spring Break Family Road Trip: San Antonio & Austin
## April 10–18 | Family of 4

---

## 1. Rental Car Recommendation

### Recommended Vehicle: **Mid-Size SUV**
Examples: Toyota RAV4, Ford Escape, Hyundai Tucson

**Why this category:**
- Comfortable seating for 4 with legroom for kids
- Ample cargo space for luggage + souvenirs
- Better visibility for kids to see the Texas scenery
- Fuel-efficient enough for budget (typically 28-32 MPG highway)

### Estimated Cost: **$350–$450** for 8 days

**One-way drop-off note:** Dropping off at a different airport (SAT → HOU) typically adds $50–$100. Budget for the higher end.

### Tips for Best Deals:

| Strategy | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Book through Costco Travel** | Often 10-20% cheaper; includes second driver free |
| **Check AutoSlash.com** | Monitors prices and rebooks if rates drop |
| **Compare SAT vs. off-airport** | Sometimes downtown locations are cheaper (but less convenient with kids + luggage) |
| **Prepay vs. pay later** | Prepaid rates save money but are less flexible |
| **Skip the rental insurance** | If your personal auto policy or credit card covers rentals |
| **Choose HOU over IAH** | HOU (Hobby) is smaller and easier to navigate; confirm your flight departs from HOU |

**Recommended rental companies for families:** Enterprise, National, or Hertz (generally better car condition and customer service)

---

## 2. Hotel Recommendations

### San Antonio — 3 Nights (April 10–13)
*Location priority: Near Riverwalk for walkability*

| Hotel | Price/Night | Total (3 nights) | Pros | Cons | Family Rating |
|-------|-------------|------------------|------|------|---------------|
| **Drury Inn & Suites Riverwalk** | ~$180 | ~$540 | Free hot breakfast, free evening "kickback" (drinks/snacks), indoor/outdoor pool, excellent Riverwalk location | Can book up fast; rooms are standard size | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Best Value |
| **Hyatt Regency San Antonio Riverwalk** | ~$220 | ~$660 | Directly on Riverwalk, rooftop pool with Alamo view, larger rooms | Pricier; resort fee ~$25/night | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Best Location |
| **Holiday Inn Express Riverwalk** | ~$150 | ~$450 | Budget-friendly, free breakfast, walkable to Riverwalk | Pool is small; slightly further from main Riverwalk attractions | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Budget Pick |

**My recommendation:** **Drury Inn & Suites Riverwalk** — The free breakfast and evening kickback (5:30–7pm with hot food and drinks) will save you $50–$80/day on meals. Kids love the pool. Location is excellent.

---

### Austin — 4 Nights (April 13–17)
*Location priority: Walkable to South Congress (SoCo) or Downtown*

| Hotel | Price/Night | Total (4 nights) | Pros | Cons | Family Rating |
|-------|-------------|------------------|------|------|---------------|
| **Hampton Inn & Suites Austin-Downtown/Convention Center** | ~$200 | ~$800 | Pool, free breakfast, walkable to Congress Ave Bridge (bats!), Lady Bird Lake trail access | Standard rooms; parking ~$30/night | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Best Overall |
| **Hotel San José (South Congress)** | ~$250 | ~$1,000 | Iconic SoCo location, trendy courtyard, walking distance to all SoCo shops | Small pool, minimalist rooms, no breakfast | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Coolest Vibe |
| **Drury Inn & Suites Austin North** | ~$160 | ~$640 | Free breakfast + evening kickback, great pool, newer property | Not downtown; 15-min drive to SoCo | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Budget Pick |

**My recommendation:** **Hampton Inn Downtown** — Perfect balance of location, amenities, and price. You can walk to Congress Avenue Bridge for the bats, Lady Bird Lake for paddleboarding, and it's a short drive/ride to everything else.

**Budget alternative:** If you loved Drury in San Antonio, the **Drury Inn Austin North** gives you the same perks at lower cost—just plan on driving everywhere.

---

## 3. Day-by-Day Itinerary

### San Antonio

---

#### **April 10 (Thursday) — Arrival Day**
*Flight arrives afternoon; kids will be tired*

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| 3:00 PM | Land at SAT, pick up rental car | Allow 45–60 min for car rental process |
| 4:30 PM | Check into hotel | Request early check-in if possible |
| 5:00 PM | **Riverwalk stroll** | Let kids stretch legs; the Riverwalk is magical at dusk |
| 6:00 PM | **Dinner at Casa Rio** | Classic Tex-Mex right on the Riverwalk; colorful umbrellas, kids' menu |
| 7:30 PM | **Rio San Antonio Cruise** | 35-minute narrated boat tour ($15 adults, $8 kids); relaxing way to see the Riverwalk without walking |
| 8:30 PM | Back to hotel, pool time | Let kids burn remaining energy |

**Vibe:** Easy, low-key evening. No pressure. Save energy for tomorrow.

---

#### **April 11 (Friday) — Full Day #1: History + Animals**
*Theme: The Alamo + San Antonio Zoo*

| Time | Activity | Details | Cost |
|------|----------|---------|------|
| 8:00 AM | Hotel breakfast | Take advantage of free breakfast! | $0 |
| 9:00 AM | **The Alamo** | Iconic Texas landmark; free to enter. Book the **Battlefield Tour** ($25/adult, $15/child) for a guided experience. Kids 8–11 love the cannon and weaponry exhibits. Allow 1.5–2 hours. | ~$80 |
| 11:30 AM | Walk to **Alamo Plaza** | Let kids explore the grounds; great photo ops |
| 12:00 PM | **Lunch at Schilo's Delicatessen** | San Antonio's oldest restaurant (since 1917); great sandwiches, famous root beer | ~$50 |
| 1:30 PM | Drive to **San Antonio Zoo** (15 min) | One of the best zoos in Texas; 750+ species. Don't miss the new Africa Live! exhibit. Train ride inside the zoo is a hit with kids. Allow 3–4 hours. | ~$100 (4 tickets) |
| 5:30 PM | Return to hotel | Pool time before dinner |
| 7:00 PM | **Dinner at Rainforest Cafe (Rivercenter Mall)** | Yes, it's a chain, but kids LOVE it. Animatronic animals, thunderstorms, and fish tanks everywhere. | ~$70 |
| 8:30 PM | Evening Riverwalk walk | Get ice cream, watch the lights |

**Day cost estimate:** ~$300

---

#### **April 12 (Saturday) — Full Day #2: Theme Park Day**
*Theme: SeaWorld San Antonio OR Natural Bridge Caverns + Morgan's Wonderland*

**Option A: SeaWorld San Antonio (Full Day)**

| Time | Activity | Details | Cost |
|------|----------|---------|------|
| 9:00 AM | Arrive at SeaWorld (opens 10 AM) | 25-minute drive from downtown | |
| 10 AM–5 PM | **SeaWorld San Antonio** | Rides, animal shows, Sesame Street Bay of Play for younger kids. Highlight: The new Catapult Falls water ride. April weather is perfect (not too hot). | ~$250 (4 tickets if bought online in advance) |
| 6:00 PM | Return to hotel | Quick pool dip |
| 7:30 PM | **Dinner at La Gloria** | Chef Johnny Hernandez's authentic Mexican street food on the Pearl complex; less touristy than Riverwalk, amazing tacos | ~$60 |

**Option B: Caves + Inclusive Playground (More Unique)**

| Time | Activity | Details | Cost |
|------|----------|---------|------|
| 9:00 AM | Drive to **Natural Bridge Caverns** (30 min) | Texas' largest show cavern; 60-minute walking tour, 180 feet underground. Kids 8–11 think it's incredible. | ~$100 (4 tickets) |
| 12:00 PM | Lunch at the cavern's café | Basic but convenient | ~$40 |
| 1:30 PM | **Morgan's Wonderland** (20 min drive) | World's first fully accessible theme park; admission is FREE for kids with disabilities, low-cost for everyone else. Incredible rides, splash pad, and truly joyful atmosphere. Even if your kids don't have disabilities, it's a beautiful experience. | ~$70 (4 tickets) |
| 5:00 PM | Return to hotel | |
| 7:00 PM | **Dinner at The Guenther House** | Beautiful historic home; famous breakfast/brunch spot also serves dinner. Gardens are lovely. | ~$60 |

**My recommendation:** If your kids love marine life and roller coasters → SeaWorld. If they're curious explorers → Natural Bridge Caverns + Morgan's Wonderland combo is unforgettable and more unique.

**Day cost estimate:** ~$300–350

---

#### **April 13 (Sunday) — Morning, then Drive to Austin**
*Quick activity before checkout*

| Time | Activity | Details |
|------|----------|---------|
| 8:00 AM | Breakfast at hotel | |
| 9:00 AM | **San Antonio Missions National Historical Park** | Drive the Mission Trail to see Mission Concepción (10 min from downtown). These are UNESCO World Heritage Sites and genuinely impressive. Free admission. 1 hour is enough. |
| 10:30 AM | Check out of hotel | |
| 11:00 AM | **Depart for Austin** | 1.5 hour drive on I-35 |

---

### Austin

---

#### **April 13 (Sunday) — Arrival in Austin**
*Arriving early afternoon*

| Time | Activity | Details | Cost |
|------|----------|---------|------|
| 12:30 PM | Arrive in Austin | |
| 1:00 PM | **Lunch on South Congress (SoCo)** | Walk the strip! Try **Hopdoddy Burger Bar** (kids love it) or **Torchy's Tacos** (Austin classic) | ~$60 |
| 2:30 PM | **SoCo shopping & exploring** | Let kids pick a souvenir at **Uncommon Objects** (quirky antiques), get boots fitted at **Allen's Boots**, and grab dessert at **Amy's Ice Creams** | ~$40 |
| 4:00 PM | Check into hotel | |
| 5:00 PM | **Lady Bird Lake Hike/Bike Trail** | Easy stroll along the water; rent bikes or scooters if kids want | $0–$50 |
| 7:45 PM | **Congress Avenue Bridge Bat Watching** | 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats emerge at dusk (around 8 PM in April). Arrive 30 min early for good spots. One of Austin's most iconic experiences. | $0 |
| 8:30 PM | **Dinner at Güero's Taco Bar** | South Congress institution; live music, great tacos, family-friendly outdoor seating | ~$65 |

**Day cost estimate:** ~$200

---

#### **April 14 (Monday) — Full Day: Science + Nature**

| Time | Activity | Details | Cost |
|------|----------|---------|------|
| 9:00 AM | **Bullock Texas State History Museum** | Three floors of Texas history with amazing artifacts, IMAX theater, and interactive exhibits. The "Story of Texas" special effects show is a must. Allow 2–3 hours. | ~$60 (4 tickets + IMAX) |
| 12:30 PM | **Lunch at Waterloo Records + food truck next door** | Browse Austin's iconic record store, then grab tacos from a food truck nearby |
| 2:00 PM | **Barton Springs Pool** | 68°F natural spring-fed pool in the heart of the city. Even in April, locals swim here. Kids 8–11 love the cold water and diving area. Lifeguards on duty. | ~$20 (4 tickets) |
| 5:00 PM | Return to hotel to change | |
| 6:30 PM | **Food Truck Park dinner — The Picnic** | On Barton Springs Road; multiple trucks, communal seating, live music. Very Austin. | ~$50 |
| 8:00 PM | Hotel pool or early night | |

**Day cost estimate:** ~$150

---

#### **April 15 (Tuesday) — Full Day: Thinkery + Hamilton Pool**

| Time | Activity | Details | Cost |
|------|----------|---------|------|
| 9:30 AM | **Thinkery Children's Museum** | Austin's premier children's museum. Designed for ages 0–11. Highlights: outdoor play area, STEM labs, water play section (bring a change of clothes!). Allow 2–3 hours. | ~$60 (4 tickets) |
| 12:30 PM | **Lunch at Kerbey Lane Cafe** | Austin institution; giant pancakes, healthy options too | ~$55 |
| 2:30 PM | **Hamilton Pool Preserve** | Stunning natural grotto with 50-foot waterfall. 45-minute drive but WORTH IT. **Reservations required** — book at least 2 weeks in advance. Swimming allowed if bacteria levels are safe. Even if not, the hike and scenery are incredible. | ~$15 (parking reservation) |
| 6:00 PM | Return to Austin | |
| 7:00 PM | **Dinner at Matt's El Rancho** | Austin Tex-Mex legend since 1952; get the Bob Armstrong Dip | ~$70 |

**Day cost estimate:** ~$200

---

#### **April 16 (Wednesday) — Full Day: Choose Your Adventure**

**Option A: Outdoors Focus — Zilker Park + Umlauf Sculpture Garden**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 9:00 AM | **Zilker Park** — rent kayaks or paddleboards on Lady Bird Lake ($30–$50/hour for a tandem kayak) |
| 12:00 PM | Picnic lunch from Whole Foods (flagship store on Lamar!) |
| 2:00 PM | **Umlauf Sculpture Garden** — small but beautiful outdoor art museum; $5/adult, kids free |
| 4:00 PM | **Peter Pan Mini Golf** — two vintage 1940s courses; quirky Austin tradition |
| 7:00 PM | **Dinner at The Salt Lick BBQ (Driftwood)** — 30-min drive; legendary Texas BBQ, BYOB, outdoor seating, live music on weekends |

**Option B: More Museums + Downtown**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 9:00 AM | **LBJ Presidential Library** — surprisingly engaging for kids; replica Oval Office, 1960s exhibits |
| 12:00 PM | Lunch at **Loro** (Asian smokehouse by the Franklin BBQ team) |
| 2:00 PM | **Walk the UT Austin campus** — beautiful grounds, see the tower |
| 4:00 PM | **HOPE Outdoor Gallery / Graffiti Park** (moved to Carson Creek Ranch) — if open; check status |
| 7:00 PM | **6th Street** (early evening) — walk the famous strip before it gets rowdy; grab dinner at **Moonshine Patio Bar & Grill** |

**My recommendation:** Option A for active families; Option B for curious/artsy families.

**Day cost estimate:** ~$180

---

#### **April 17 (Thursday) — Checkout & Drive to Houston**

| Time | Activity | Details |
|------|----------|---------|
| 8:00 AM | Hotel breakfast | |
| 9:00 AM | **Checkout** | |
| 9:30 AM | **One last Austin stop: Jo's Coffee on SoCo** | Famous "I Love You So Much" mural for a family photo |
| 10:00 AM | **Depart for Houston** | 2.5–3 hour drive on TX-71 → I-10 |
| 12:30 PM | **Lunch stop in Buc-ee's (Bastrop or Katy)** | Texas institution! Massive gas station, incredible snacks, cleanest restrooms in America. Kids will be amazed. |
| 2:00 PM | Arrive in Houston | Check into airport hotel if needed, or explore |
| 3:00 PM | **Optional: Space Center Houston** (if time allows) | Only 30 min from Hobby Airport. Incredible NASA facility with moon rocks, shuttle replica, tram tour. Even 2 hours is worthwhile. | ~$120 (4 tickets) |
| 6:00 PM | **Dinner near airport** | Pappadeaux (Houston seafood institution) or grab something casual |
| | **Stay near HOU airport** | Recommend: Marriott Houston Hobby Airport (~$130/night) for easy morning departure |

---

#### **April 18 (Friday) — Departure Day**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Early AM | Drop off rental car at HOU (Hobby) |
| | Flight home to Seattle |

## 4. Top 5 Must-Do Activities (Kids 8–11)

### San Antonio

| Rank | Activity | Why Kids Love It |
|------|----------|------------------|
| 1 | **The Alamo + Battlefield Tour** | Real history brought to life; cannonballs, muskets, defenders' stories |
| 2 | **San Antonio Zoo** | Huge variety, train ride, Africa Live! exhibit |
| 3 | **Riverwalk Boat Tour** | Magical at night; relaxing but engaging |
| 4 | **Natural Bridge Caverns** | Underground adventure; feels like exploring a secret world |
| 5 | **SeaWorld San Antonio** | Rides + animals; perfect for this age group |

### Austin

| Rank | Activity | Why Kids Love It |
|------|----------|------------------|
| 1 | **Congress Avenue Bridge Bats** | 1.5 million bats! Free, unforgettable, perfectly timed for dusk |
| 2 | **Barton Springs Pool** | Natural cold spring; feels like swimming in nature |
| 3 | **Thinkery Children's Museum** | Hands-on STEM + outdoor play; designed for exactly their ages |
| 4 | **Hamilton Pool Preserve** | Stunning waterfall grotto; adventure vibes |
| 5 | **Lady Bird Lake Kayaking/Paddleboarding** | Active fun on the water in the heart of the city |

---

## 5. Driving Routes

### San Antonio → Austin

| Detail | Information |
|--------|-------------|
| **Best Route** | I-35 North (direct) |
| **Distance** | 80 miles |
| **Drive Time** | 1 hour 20 min – 1 hour 45 min (depending on traffic) |
| **Traffic Tip** | Avoid leaving San Antonio during morning rush (7–9 AM). Sunday midday should be smooth. |
| **Worth stopping?** | **New Braunfels** (30 min north of SA) — cute German-Texas town. If you want to stretch legs, walk the downtown square. Otherwise, drive straight through. |
| **Gas** | Fill up before leaving San Antonio; prices similar in both cities |

### Austin → Houston (Hobby Airport)

| Detail | Information |
|--------|-------------|
| **Best Route** | TX-71 East → I-10 East → TX-288 South (to Hobby) |
| **Distance** | ~165 miles |
| **Drive Time** | 2 hours 30 min – 3 hours |
| **Traffic Tip** | Houston traffic can be brutal. Leaving Austin by 10 AM gets you to Houston by 1 PM, well before rush hour. |
| **Must-Stop** | **Buc-ee's in Bastrop** (45 min from Austin) — the quintessential Texas road trip stop. Massive gas station, incredible brisket sandwiches, beaver nuggets (addictive snacks), and the cleanest restrooms you've ever seen. Kids will want to spend 30+ minutes here. |
| **Gas** | Fill up at Buc-ee's; prices are competitive and it's convenient |

### 🚨 Budget Alert: You're ~$600–$800 Over Budget

**Here's how to get back to $3,000:**

| Cut This | Savings | Impact |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Skip SeaWorld** | -$250 | High impact; replace with free/cheap alternatives (see below) |
| **Skip Space Center Houston** | -$120 | Medium impact; you can always visit Houston another time |
| **Choose Drury Inn Austin (north) instead of Hampton Downtown** | -$160 | Requires driving; loses walkability |
| **Cook some meals (Airbnb instead of hotel)** | -$100–200 | Trade-off: lose breakfast; gain kitchen |
| **Pack lunches some days** | -$100 | Stop at H-E-B (Texas grocery chain) for picnic supplies |

**My Recommended Cuts to Hit $3,000:**

1. **Skip SeaWorld** (-$250) — Replace with:
   - **San Antonio Botanical Garden** ($60 for family; beautiful, peaceful)
   - **Japanese Tea Garden** (FREE; stunning)
   - **Extra Riverwalk time/swimming at hotel**

2. **Make Space Center Houston optional** (-$120) — Only do it if kids are space-obsessed

3. **Eat lighter lunches 3 days** (-$60) — Buc-ee's brisket sandwiches, H-E-B deli, hotel leftovers

**Revised Total: ~$2,600–$2,800** ✅

## 7. Practical Tips

### Best Apps for Road Trips with Kids

| App | What It Does | Why You Need It |
|-----|--------------|-----------------|
| **GasBuddy** | Find cheapest gas prices | Save $5–$10 on the trip |
| **Roadtrippers** | Plan route + discover roadside attractions | Kids can help find cool stops |
| **Spotify/Apple Music** | Music + podcasts | Create a family road trip playlist before you go |
| **Libby** | Free audiobooks from your library | Download 2–3 audiobooks for the drives |
| **AllTrails** | Hiking trail maps | Great for Hamilton Pool and Lady Bird Lake |
| **Google Maps (offline)** | Navigation even without signal | Download Texas map before leaving |

### What to Pack in the Car

**For the Kids:**
- [ ] Tablets/iPads with downloaded movies (Netflix offline mode!)
- [ ] Headphones (2 pairs minimum)
- [ ] Activity books, coloring supplies
- [ ] Snack bag (individually portioned)
- [ ] Refillable water bottles (4)
- [ ] Travel pillow for naps
- [ ] Plastic bags (for trash and wet swimsuits)

**For the Parents:**
- [ ] Phone chargers + car USB adapter
- [ ] Portable phone charger (for bat watching, etc.)
- [ ] Paper towels/wipes
- [ ] First aid kit
- [ ] Sunscreen (Texas sun is strong in April!)
- [ ] Hats for everyone
- [ ] Light rain jackets (April can have pop-up showers)
- [ ] Reusable shopping bags (Texas charges for bags)

**For Texas Specifically:**
- [ ] Swimsuits (for Barton Springs, Hamilton Pool, hotel pools)
- [ ] Water shoes (rocky bottoms at natural swimming spots)
- [ ] Light layers (mornings can be cool, afternoons warm)

### April Events & Festivals to Know About

| Event | Dates | Location | Notes |
|-------|-------|----------|-------|
| **Fiesta San Antonio** | April 18–28, 2024 (varies yearly) | San Antonio | HUGE 10-day festival; you'll catch the beginning if dates align. Parades, food, music everywhere. Check 2025 dates! |
| **Austin Food & Wine Festival** | Mid-April (varies) | Austin | Mostly adult-focused but good restaurant energy in town |
| **Easter Weekend** | Check 2025 date | Both cities | If Easter falls during your trip, some attractions may have special hours or events |
| **Bat Season** | March–October | Austin | You're visiting at perfect time; colony is active |

**Weather Expectation (April):**
- Highs: 75–85°F
- Lows: 55–65°F
- Chance of afternoon thunderstorms
- Generally sunny and pleasant—best time to visit Texas!

**Have an amazing trip!** Texas Hill Country in April is absolutely beautiful, the food is incredible, and both San Antonio and Austin are wonderfully kid-friendly cities. Your 8 and 11-year-old are at the perfect ages to appreciate the Alamo, love the bats, and remember this trip forever.

Safe travels! 🤠
